caption:
The AI race is arriving just as the energy transition enters its most consequential phase.
 
Countries are trying to decarbonize, expand access, strengthen resilience and meet rising electricity demand all at once. Now AI adds another layer: demand for compute, data centres, water, cooling and firm clean power.
 
But the AI-energy question is bigger than electricity consumption. It is about whether countries can use AI to strengthen both sides of the energy equation: cleaner, more reliable supply and energy use that is more efficient, flexible and productive for development.
 
The word intelligence comes from the Latin "inter-legere": to choose between, to discern, to make connections. That is the choice before us: will AI accelerate resilience, productivity and opportunity, or concentrate value in the hands of a few?
 
This is what we explore, together with Amir Lebdioui and Angel Melguizo, in our new UNDP -TIDE Centre, University of Oxford Centre paper: "The Energy Sprint of the AI Race: A Green Window of Opportunity for Developing Countries?" 
📖 https://lnkd.in/gUFFVVgS

At UNDP, we are supporting countries to connect energy, data and digital systems into one people-centred development pathway. What do you see as the biggest opportunity, and the biggest risk, at the intersection of AI, energy and development?
